questions.stem: GDPR requires personal data breach notification to the supervisory authority within:

choices.B: 72 hours of becoming aware, where feasible

questions.explanation: GDPR Article 33 requires notification within 72 hours of becoming aware, unless the breach is unlikely to result in risk to individuals.

choices.B: Encryption of both data and system firmware
choices.C: Ransomware with a DDoS attack on the victim
choices.D: File encryption (pay to decrypt) with data theft (pay or we publish stolen data)

questions.explanation: Double extortion eliminates 'restore from backup' as a complete remedy, victims still face data exposure even if they restore encrypted files.

choices.A: Maximum acceptable downtime before business impact becomes unacceptable
choices.B: Maximum tolerable data loss measured in time
choices.C: How long a backup takes to complete
choices.D: The time between attack and detection

questions.explanation: RTO is the maximum acceptable downtime. RPO is the maximum acceptable data loss. Together they drive backup frequency and recovery architecture.

choices.A: Three daily, two weekly, one monthly backup
choices.B: Three copies encrypted with two different keys one stored offline
choices.C: Three cloud regions, two ISPs, one local copy
choices.D: Three copies on two different media types with one copy stored offsite

questions.explanation: 3-2-1: 3 copies, 2 different media, 1 offsite. This eliminates single points of failure, a fire destroying local storage still leaves the offsite copy.

questions.stem: Immutable backups protect against ransomware because:

choices.A: They encrypt the backup before ransomware can
choices.B: Data cannot be modified or deleted for a defined retention period, even with admin credentials
choices.C: They store backups with no network connectivity
choices.D: They run every minute to minimise data loss

questions.explanation: Immutable backups (write-once storage, cloud object lock) cannot be modified or deleted, preserving recovery capability even when an attacker has admin-level access.

questions.stem: A tabletop exercise for incident response is:

choices.A: Deploying actual malware in a controlled environment
choices.C: A simulated discussion-based walk-through of an incident scenario testing decision-making without disrupting operations
choices.D: Full red team attack simulation against live infrastructure

questions.explanation: A tabletop exercise is discussion-based, participants walk through a hypothetical scenario, testing plans and communication without technical execution or production risk.

questions.stem: A Data Processing Agreement (DPA) under GDPR is required when:

choices.A: An organisation stores personal data in the cloud
choices.B: An employee accesses personal data remotely
choices.C: Personal data is shared with a third-party processor, specifying security obligations and breach notification requirements
choices.D: An organisation first collects data from EU citizens

questions.explanation: GDPR Article 28 requires a DPA between controllers and processors specifying purpose, duration, security measures, and sub-processor requirements.

questions.stem: Breach notifications to affected individuals must include:

choices.A: The attacker's identity and how they were found
choices.B: Description of the breach, data categories affected, likely consequences, and steps individuals can take
choices.C: A legal waiver for the organisation
choices.D: Full technical details of how controls were bypassed

questions.explanation: Breach notifications must include: breach description, data categories affected, likely consequences, measures taken, and self-protection advice.

choices.B: How long it takes to restore from backup
choices.C: Maximum tolerable data loss measured in time, how old the recovered data can be

questions.explanation: RPO is the maximum acceptable data loss, 'how old can our recovered data be?' It drives backup frequency decisions.

questions.stem: Which controls make backups most resilient against ransomware?

choices.A: Frequent daily backups to the same network location
choices.B: Storing backups only in the cloud
choices.C: Encrypting backups with the same key as production data
choices.D: Immutable offsite backups combined with 3-2-1 strategy and tested recovery procedures

questions.explanation: Immutable + offsite + tested recovery covers all ransomware scenarios: attackers cannot delete immutable backups, offsite protects against physical damage, and tested procedures ensure recovery actually works.
